config.title: ccas settings:
config.keys: up/down choose - Enter/space/left/right change - +/- step - q quit
config.bad_value: '{value}' is not a valid value for {key}
config.edit_via_cli: set this one from the command line: ccas config {key} <value>
config.help_auto-switch: when a session runs into its limit, restart it on another account and continue the same conversation
config.help_auto-switch-strategy: how the target slot is chosen; "by limits" takes the least loaded one and falls back to slot order when no data is available
config.help_auto-switch-threshold: how full the 5-hour window must be before the account counts as spent (50-100)
config.help_auto-switch-max: how many times in a row a session may move before it stops trying (1-10)
config.help_auto-switch-max-wait: when every account is spent, how long a session may wait for the nearest reset before giving up (0 - never wait)
config.help_auto-switch-confirm: ask the API for limits before moving - filters out transient 429s, but needs a connection
config.help_auto-switch-restore-mode: pass --permission-mode on relaunch so plan mode and friends survive the move
config.help_auto-switch-prompt: sent to the restored session right after relaunch; empty means send nothing
config.help_language: language of ccas messages; the CCAS_LANG variable wins over it
config.help_claude-path: the original Claude Code executable the wrapper launches
hooks.none: no external handlers. Add one: ccas hooks add <event> <command>
hooks.no_such: there is no handler {index}. List: ccas hooks list
config.help_hooks-bus: hand every claude session a settings file that reports its hook events to ccas over a local port; needed by the external handlers and the Telegram transport
config.bad_token: that does not look like a bot token (expected <digits>:<letters>, as @BotFather gives it)
config.help_telegram-token: the token @BotFather issued; the bot id is the part before the colon
config.help_telegram-console: a session started with /claude gets its own console window on the PC, mirroring the chat and taking input too
config.help_telegram-prompt-timeout: how long a question or permission prompt waits in the chat before it is declined so claude can go on (0 - wait forever)
tg.no_token: no Telegram bot token. Set one: ccas config telegram-token <token>, or pass --tg-token
tg.token_held_locally: this bot is already polled by ccas process {pid} on this machine; start the daemon or use another bot
tg.token_busy: Telegram refused the poll: {reason}. Another ccas (maybe on another machine) owns this bot; the session ends.
tg.login_needed: slot {slot} has no credentials yet. Run `claude {slot}` in a terminal, log in, then start the chat session.
tg.started: 🟢 claude on slot {slot} ({label}) 📁 {cwd} 🏷 {alias} · session {session} /help for the commands
tg.console_ready: [ccas] session {session} ready, model {model}. This window is a log; the conversation is in Telegram. To continue in a terminal: claude, then /resume.
tg.not_running: claude is not running any more: {error}
tg.state_limited: waiting out a limit, slot {slot} opens at {opens}
tg.help:
Address me with {alias} at the start of every message; {alias}! interrupts what I am doing and takes the message at once.
Commands: {commands}
Modes: {modes} (now {mode}) — the mark on each of my answers is the mode it was written in.
Several commands may open one message: {alias} /new /plan <prompt>.
/new starts a fresh session, /clear does that and takes this conversation out of the chat, /exit leaves the plan and my last answer and closes.
!<cmd> runs a shell command in the session directory and shows it to claude.
Everything else is sent to claude as is (slash commands included).
tg.shell_timeout: command did not finish in {seconds} s
tg.cd_bad: no such directory, or outside the allowed roots: {path}
tg.switch_bad: no usable slot '{target}'. See: ccas list
tg.switch_none: no other slot with quota left
tg.limit_waiting: ⏳ no account is free. Slot {slot} ({label}) opens first, at {opens} — I will wait for it and carry on there
tg.limit_wait_queued: got it, I will send this after the reset at {opens}
tg.limit_over: ▶️ the limit is over, carrying on with slot {slot}
tg.perm_denied_reason: The user denied this in the Telegram chat.
tg.prompt_multi_hint: several answers allowed; press Done when finished
tg.prompt_type_answer: type your answer as the next message
tg.prompt_pick_one: pick at least one option first
tg.prompt_gone: this question has already been answered
tg.prompt_timed_out_reason: No answer arrived from the Telegram chat in time.
cli.help.daemon: the Telegram daemon: polls the bot and starts sessions on /claude
cli.help.daemon_status: is it running, and which sessions it feeds
cli.help.telegram_test: check the token and send a test message to the chat

daemon.already_running: a poller for this bot is already running (pid {pid})
daemon.listening: ccas daemon: bot {bot}, port {port}. Watching profiles: {profiles}. Everything else waits to be raised by hand.
daemon.token_busy: Telegram says another process polls this bot: {reason}. If that is another PC, give it its own bot.

daemon.stop_failed: the daemon did not stop; kill the process by hand
daemon.status_unreachable: daemon: the record is there but the port does not answer
daemon.status_lock_elsewhere: the bot token is held by another process (pid {pid})
daemon.help:
/<alias> <text> — talk to that profile's agent; /<alias>! <text> interrupts it first
/<alias> /claude [slot] [-C dir] [claude args] — start that profile in a console window on the PC
/claude [-P id | -n alias] … — the same, choosing the profile by id or alias
/claude mcp list, /claude -p … — run once and show the output
/projects — known project directories as buttons
/cd <dir>, /pwd, /ls [dir] — the directory new sessions start in
/sessions — sessions alive in this chat
Profiles here: {aliases}
daemon.button_expired: that button belongs to a session that is gone
daemon.cd_done: 📁 new sessions in this chat start in {path}
daemon.no_projects: claude has not recorded any project directories yet
daemon.projects_title: Projects (page {page}/{pages}) — 📁 picks the directory, ▶ starts a session there
daemon.launching: 🚀 starting claude in {cwd} (profile {name}); a console window opens on the PC
telegram.test_message: ✅ ccas is connected to this chat
telegram.test_no_chats: no profile names a chat yet: ccas profile add <alias> --chat <id>
doctor.hooks_bus_on: hook bus is on: claude sessions report their events to ccas ({handlers} external handlers)
doctor.hooks_bus_off: hook bus is off (ccas config hooks-bus on)
doctor.telegram_unset: Telegram transport is not set up (ccas config telegram-token, telegram-chat)
doctor.daemon_not_running: profiles {profiles} expect the daemon, but it is not running (ccas daemon start)

doctor.autostart_missing: the daemon is expected but is not registered to start at login (ccas profile set <name> --daemon on)
doctor.upgrade_pending: a newer ccas is waiting to replace the shim ({names}): close every claude session and run ccas once more

profile.hint: Create: ccas profile add <alias> [--chat <id>] [--cwd <dir>]. Change: ccas profile set <id|alias> [--alias <new>] [--cwd <dir>] [--chat <id>] [--slot N] [--mode plan] [--daemon on] [--multi on] [--debug on] [--expanded on] [--users …] [--args "…"]. Raise by hand: claude -t telegram -P <id>
config.help_telegram-max-sessions: how many claude sessions one profile may hold at the same time; with per-person sessions a busy group reaches this quickly
daemon.not_running: profile {name} is not running. Start it on the PC (claude -t telegram -P {id}), or {name} /claude here, or let the daemon raise it: ccas profile set {id} --daemon on
daemon.already_up: profile {name} is already running in this chat
